prompts.satelliteLayers:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: a premium 16:9 cinematic science film END KEYFRAME for a Korean environmental engineering company website
Reference image role: factual geography reference ONLY. Use the Korean peninsula and adjacent China/Japan coastlines from this actual platform screenshot. Do not reproduce its dashboard, type, sidebar or UI. Data colors in the artwork are conceptual and must not imply verified results
Primary scene: a believable Earth viewed from low orbit centered on the Korean peninsula. China to its west, Japanese archipelago to its east and south east, Jeju south of the peninsula. Correct land and sea relationships. Gently curved Earth occupies the lower two thirds, warm natural land colors, desaturated navy seas, restrained atmosphere and sparse realistic clouds
At the upper left a modest realistically constructed Earth-observation satellite with paired solar panels, viewing instrument pointing toward Korea, no visible laser beam
Main visual: directly above the Korea region of the Earth, THREE clearly separated thin 2D geospatial map sheets rise into the air in a precise aligned stack. Each sheet shows the SAME Korean peninsula coast mask and SAME regional bounding rectangle including adjacent East China Sea, Yellow Sea and East Sea; all sheets stay spatially registered above that region. They are flat two-dimensional geospatial fields, not cubes, not generic glass cards. Thin neutral edges, no glowing outlines
Bottom sheet: sea surface temperature field, muted thermal amber/rust through cool teal, smooth physically plausible broad fronts in water only
Middle sheet: surface salinity field, subtle desaturated indigo/blue-green gradients in water only, lighter estuarine plume near coast
Top sheet: chlorophyll field, olive to restrained yellow-green patchiness concentrated along shelf/coastal water, deep ocean darker
Land remains neutral dark charcoal consistently masked on all THREE sheets. Leave generous air between sheets so each layer reads distinctly. Do not paint data across land. Layer fields are illustrative, no numeric scales, no values, no charts, no invented boundaries
Composition: an elegant 3/4 oblique perspective looking down on the globe and sheet stack, Korea must remain recognizable, satellite small but readable, background almost black. All important objects within central 80 percent crop safety. Cinematic scientific art direction, sophisticated physically based rendering
Future animation continuity: this is the final frame of a 9 second shot where an already-present satellite observes and these three maps successively lift from Earth's surface, maintaining the exact same camera angle, geography and scale. Stable unbroken geography is critical
No words, letters, labels, icons, fake UI, neon cyan, blue flow lines, decorative wireframes, excessive stars, ring trails, lasers, monstrous satellite, sci-fi city, infographic arrows or grids covering the ocean. Detailed, restrained, technically literate visual concept

prompts.coastalModel:
Use case: style-transfer / scientific concept
Input role: the supplied GeoSR coastal-survey image is the STRICT GEOMETRY REFERENCE for a Korean coast. This is a company website's environmental modelling film END KEYFRAME, 16:9
Preserve the exact geographic arrangement and proportions of the curved sandy beach, shore road, buildings, trees, connected breakwaters, their bent heads, separate upper harbor opening and visible nearshore rock patches. Do not invent islands, move the harbor entrance, extend a breakwater across the navigation opening or add foreign architecture
Reinterpret this SAME existing viewpoint as an exceptionally polished coastal wave modelling visualization: most of the view stays photoreal with natural green-blue coastal water and Korean land textures; a very restrained few parallel soft physical wave crests approach from open sea on the right, bend naturally as they meet the nearshore shallows, and diffract softly around the breakwater head. The sheltered water behind the breakwater stays quieter, waves must not travel through concrete or across dry land. Fine low-contrast white wave crests in water, not glowing or cyan flow lines
A small central water patch subtly reveals a neutral slate unstructured numerical mesh beneath the surface, following this same surface perspective, only in that patch, very fine understated edges
Use calm credible coastal-engineering presentation, natural overcast daylight, realistic concrete tetrapods, believable small-town scale, accurate land/water mask. Preserve reference geography over visual novelty
No plots, axes, arrows, labels, numbers, UI, people, drones, satellite, cutaway island, futuristic hologram, neon lines or giant waves
This is a conceptual numerical-wave illustration, NOT a reconstruction of observed wave data or a verified project output
Future animation: fixed camera; begin from the unchanged reference geography with still water, then wave crests enter gradually over 6 seconds and the single local mesh patch fades in near the end. Keep all fixed land and built structures identical between every frame
